papers.title: Optimization as Estimation with Gaussian Processes in Bandit Settings
papers.abstract: Recently, there has been rising interest in Bayesian optimization -- the optimization of an unknown function with assumptions usually expressed by a Gaussian Process (GP) prior. We study an optimization strategy that directly uses an estimate of the argmax of the function. This strategy offers both practical and theoretical advantages: no tradeoff parameter needs to be selected, and, moreover, we establish close connections to the popular GP-UCB and GP-PI strategies. Our approach can be understood as automatically and adaptively trading off exploration and exploitation in GP-UCB and GP-PI. We illustrate the effects of this adaptive tuning via bounds on the regret as well as an extensive empirical evaluation on robotics and vision tasks, demonstrating the robustness of this strategy for a range of performance criteria.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于高斯过程的贝叶斯优化方法，未涉及FEA替代建模、约束优化或生物力学设计中的不确定性量化。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address constraint handling, uncertainty quantification in the context of FEA surrogate modeling, or application to implant/biomechanics design; its validation is on robotics and vision tasks, not on expensive simulation sampling for structural mechanics.

summary_en.motivation: This paper investigates a Bayesian optimization strategy that directly estimates the argmax of the objective function without requiring a trade-off parameter.
summary_en.method: The proposed method uses the Gaussian process posterior to estimate the location of the maximum, automatically balancing exploration and exploitation.
summary_en.result: The approach establishes theoretical connections to GP-UCB and GP-PI, and demonstrates robust performance across robotics and vision tasks.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through empirical evaluation on robotics and vision tasks.

papers.title: Phase Formation, Thermal Stability and Mechanical Properties of a Cu-Al-Ni-Mn Shape Memory Alloy Prepared by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is an additive manufacturing process used to produce parts with complex geometries layer by layer. This rapid solidification method allows fabricating samples in a non-equilibrium state and with refined microstructure. In this work, this method is used to fabricate 3 mm diameter rods of a Cu-based shape memory alloy. The phase formation, thermal stability and mechanical properties were investigated and correlated. Samples with a relative density higher than 92% and without cracks were obtained. A single monoclinic martensitic phase was formed with average grain size ranging between 28 to 36 μm. The samples exhibit a reverse martensitic transformation temperature around 106 ± 2 °C and a large plasticity in compression (around 15±1%) with a typical “double-yielding” behaviour.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究SLM制备Cu基形状记忆合金的相形成与力学性能。
summary_zh.method: 采用选择性激光熔化制备Cu-Al-Ni-Mn合金棒材并进行表征。
summary_zh.result: 获得高密度、无裂纹的单相马氏体组织，压缩塑性达15%。
summary_zh.validation: 通过压缩测试验证力学性能。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate phase formation, thermal stability, and mechanical properties of a Cu-based shape memory alloy fabricated by selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Cu-Al-Ni-Mn alloy rods were fabricated by SLM and characterized for phase, transformation temperature, and compressive behavior.
summary_en.result: Dense, crack-free samples with a single martensitic phase and large compressive plasticity (~15%) were obtained.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical properties were validated through compression testing.
